title: Deliver task history as advisory context, not executable rules
context: Earlier agent work (lessons learned, rules applied, decisions saved, checks passed) is valuable context before re-touching a file, but should not constrain the next agent's autonomy or create permanent obligations. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.'); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Tasks are delivered as supplements (advisory history sharing the brief's budget, withheld on time-travel, never ranked memory records). Each appears as one bounded line: identity, timestamp, state, title, lessons received, rules applied, what was saved, last check result, violations, denials, files. Newest first, limited to 3 per file. Agents see the history but are not obligated to repeat, skip, or follow it; pure context.
consequences: Next agent has visibility into what was tried and verified, reducing blind rediscovery
Agent retains full autonomy to apply different approaches; history is not prescriptive
Task supplements compete for token budget alongside constraints and decisions
Task context is withheld from time-travel queries to avoid muddying historical state with evolving graph knowledge
Knowledge accumulates in persistent graph memory but creates no permanent obligations
alternatives_rejected: Deliver tasks as ranked memory or persistent constraints (would lock future agents into prior decisions, losing autonomy)
Include all task history unbounded (would exhaust context budget and overwhelm with noise)
Include tasks in time-travel views (would muddy historical reconstruction)
Make task history rule-based instead of advisory (would sacrifice agent freedom for determinism)
